hints.title: Bipartite Grid Structure
hints.text: A grid graph is bipartite with partition defined by whether row plus column coordinate is even or odd.

hints.title: Vertex Cover Equivalence
hints.text: Removing an adjacent pair of ones requires choosing at least one endpoint to flip to zero.

hints.title: Konig Maximum Matching
hints.text: By Konig theorem, the minimum vertex cover equals the maximum cardinality bipartite matching.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.time: O(V * E) bipartite matching via Kuhn algorithm
complexity.space: O(V + E) bipartite graph adjacency table
variables: V: number of one cells in grid
complexity.notes: By Konig theorem, the minimum vertex cover in a bipartite graph equals its maximum matching.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Greedy flipping or branch and bound leads to exponential states.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Grid adjacency naturally forms a bipartite graph by cell parity (r + c) % 2.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize this as minimum vertex cover on a bipartite grid and apply maximum matching.
